slides: Let's continue with divisibility, and build signs for more divisors.

slides.say: Six is a strange one, because it has no sign of its own. But six is two times three. So a number that divides by two and also by three is divisible by six. Two hundred thirty-four is even, so it divides by two. Its digit sum is two plus three plus four, which is nine, so it divides by three. So two hundred thirty-four is divisible by six.
at: But six is two times three

slides.say: Now a non-example, a hundred thirty-five. Its digit sum is one plus three plus five, nine, so it divides by three. But it's odd, so it doesn't divide by two. So it's not divisible by six.

We can build other divisors the same way. Fifteen is three times five. Five hundred ten ends in zero, so it divides by five, and its digit sum is five plus one plus zero, which is six, so it divides by three. So five hundred ten is divisible by fifteen.
at: Five hundred ten ends in zero

slides.say: Twelve is three times four, eighteen is two times nine, and twenty-four is three times eight. Check each part with its own sign. The two parts must not share a divisor bigger than one. Then, if the number divides by both parts, it divides by the big number.
at: must not share a divisor bigger than one

slides.say: But careful. Why not split twelve as two times six? Look at eighteen. Eighteen divides by two and by six, but eighteen is not divisible by twelve. Six is two times three, so two and six share a two. That's why this check doesn't work. Three and four share no divisor bigger than one, so for twelve we use three times four.
at: Eighteen divides by two and by six
eighteen is not divisible by twelve

slides.say: Eleven is the hardest one. For a two-digit number it's easy, the same digit twice: twenty-two, thirty-three, fifty-five, ninety-nine.

For a three-digit number there are two ways. The first way: take the number made by the first two digits, and subtract the last digit. Four hundred eighteen. Forty-one minus eight is thirty-three, and thirty-three divides by eleven, so four hundred eighteen divides by eleven. Four hundred twenty-seven. Forty-two minus seven is thirty-five, which doesn't divide by eleven, so four hundred twenty-seven doesn't either.

The second way: add the two outer digits, and subtract the middle digit. Four hundred eighteen again. Four plus eight is twelve, and twelve minus one is eleven. For a three-digit number, when the result is zero or eleven, the number divides by eleven.
at: when the result is zero or eleven

slides.say: For longer numbers, go digit by digit with plus, minus, plus, minus. The rule is that the result divides by eleven, and zero counts too. One thousand three hundred thirty-one. One, minus three, plus three, minus one, is zero, so it divides by eleven. Four hundred eighty-two. Four, minus eight, plus two, is minus two. Minus two doesn't divide by eleven, so four hundred eighty-two doesn't either.
at: The rule is that the result

slides.say: Most exam numbers are simple, like a hundred forty-three or a hundred sixty-five, but now you're ready for harder ones too.

Why do we need these signs? Many exam word problems are really about divisibility. For example, if a quarter of a group wear hats, the size of the group must divide by four, because you can't have a quarter of a person. The signs let us check the answer choices fast, and you'll see questions like this right after this lesson. [pause] I'll see you in the next part.
